I'm working out how much wet paint the four panels need: at 65 µm dry film thickness and 50% solids, that's about 15.6 ml per panel, so roughly 62.4 ml before any transfer losses or overspray.

The default settings would lay down about 250 µm wet, roughly 125 µm dry, which is too thick and risks sag, so I'll need to reduce the flow. The gun also hasn't been cleaned, so I'm planning to clean it and test on a card before spraying the panels. I'll check the QC configuration as well.

turns.reasoning:
The profile looks lopsided, with the peak at -20 mm and a slight skew that might mean the nozzle is partly dirty. I'm checking the card camera for the fan width, then summing the profile at 20 mm spacing to get the integral, which works out to about 38 once divided by the 50 mm pitch.

Next I'm checking whether the asymmetry points to a dirty nozzle, and I'm weighing the film thickness at 65 µm, which would mean a 30 mm pitch or a higher flow rate. Overlapping at 30 mm should even out the profile, though I still want to confirm that by viewing the card image.

I've settled on a flow of 150, a pitch of 30, and a speed of 400, with a margin of about 80 so the fan covers the edges. Each panel works out to roughly 56 ml, so four panels need 224 ml against a 268 ml pot. That fits, though it's tight, and a margin of 60 would change the line count.

Trying a 60 margin would drop the total to about 182 ml with a bit of edge loss, so I'm leaning toward 70. Rather than settle that on paper, I'll spray one panel, gauge a few points including the corners, and adjust from there. Each panel should take about 25 seconds plus the 60-second flash.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the bracket plates of job J-2219 (2219-1, 2219-2, 2219-3, 2219-4), 400 x 300 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of zinc-rich primer ZR-2; `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes
